edits.old: Dynamic mapping is not intrinsically an anti-pattern: MongoDB recommends it for unknown or frequently changing fields and experimentation, while documenting its size and performance costs. edits.new: Dynamic mapping is not intrinsically an anti-pattern: MongoDB documents it for fields that change regularly or are unknown, while warning that it can index many unique fields, which occupies more disk space and may be less performant. evidence.quote: Dynamic mappings might result in indexing a high number of unique fields, which occupies more disk space and might be less performant. Only use dynamic mappings if you need to index fields that change regularly or that are unknown.
Dynamic mappings are useful when you're just getting started with Atlas Search or if your schema changes regularly. However, they take up more space compared to static mappings.

evidence.quote: MongoDB Search supports eventual consistency and does not provide any stronger consistency guarantees. This means that data inserted into a MongoDB collection and indexed by MongoDB Search will not be available immediately for `$search` queries.
MongoDB Search reads data from MongoDB [change streams](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/changeStreams.md#std-label-changeStreams) and indexes that data in an asynchronous process.

For transactions with heavy reads after writes, we recommend [`$regex`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/regex.md#mongodb-query-op.-regex). For [`$search`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/search/query/aggregation-stages/search.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-search), reads after writes should be rare.

edits.rationale: The MongoDB Search index-performance page states that Search is eventually consistent and that inserted data is not immediately available to $search queries, since indexing is asynchronous via change streams. The query-performance page recommends $regex (a normal database query) rather than $search for transactions with heavy reads after writes. Together these support the claim; the eventual-consistency source is the index-performance page, not the originally cited page alone.
